findings.title: OAuth `state` parameter uses static `pipeline.signature` instead of a per-session random token
findings.body: `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` uses `pipeline.signature` as the OAuth2 `state` parameter (line 402) and validates `request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature` on callback (line 412). However, `pipeline.signature` is computed only from the module and class names of the pipeline views (`"9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3"`), so it is a static constant across all users, organizations, and sessions. Because `state` is not bound to the user's session, an attacker can start the OAuth flow with their own GitHub account, capture the callback URL with their `code` and the constant `state`, and via login CSRF bind their own GitHub login as `github_authenticated_user` in a victim's pipeline.

findings.title: Unchecked `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` access raises `KeyError` when `sender` is missing
findings.body: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes `"sender"` is always present in `integration.metadata`. However, `"sender"` is only added to `metadata` by the `installation` webhook, and when a pipeline completes, `finish_pipeline()` calls `build_integration(self.state)` (where `self.state` does not contain `"sender"`) and `ensure_integration()` overwrites `integration.metadata` without `"sender"`. If an organization later uninstalls the integration in Sentry (which deletes the `OrganizationIntegration` but leaves the `Integration` record active) and attempts to reinstall it, or if the `Integration` was created before this change, `integration.metadata["sender"]` will raise an unhandled `KeyError` (HTTP 500).

findings.title: `Integration.objects.get` queries by `external_id` without filtering by `provider`
findings.body: Lines 478 and 494 call `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, ...)` without filtering by `provider=GitHubIntegrationProvider.key`. The `Integration` model is only unique on `(provider, external_id)`, not on `external_id` alone. If another integration provider has an `Integration` with the same `external_id`, `Integration.objects.get` will either return the wrong provider's integration or raise an unhandled `Integration.MultipleObjectsReturned` exception.

findings.title: `test_installation_not_found` uses a stale pipeline `state` signature and no longer tests 404 handling
findings.body: Adding `OAuthLoginView` to `get_pipeline_views()` changed the pipeline signature from `ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05` to `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`. `test_installation_not_found` still sends `"state": "ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05"`, which causes `OAuthLoginView` to fail early on the `state != pipeline.signature` check and return `"Invalid installation request."` before `GitHubInstallation` or `build_integration` is ever reached. As a result, the mocked 404 on `GET /app/installations/{self.installation_id}` is never called in this test.
